nodes.name: CoPh-Phen axial coordination and pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: NC octahedrons derived from ZIF-8 used as support. CoPh (cobalt protoporphyrin) with lower thermal stability, axially coordinated with 1,10-phenanthroline (Phen), pyrolyzed to form single-atomic Co-N5/NC. Lower thermal stability of CoPh facilitates formation of five-coordinated Co sites.
nodes.source_text: The NC octahedrons derived from zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-8) were used as support for CoPh and CoPc axially coordinated with 1,10-phenanthroline (Phen) and were subsequently pyrolyzed to single-atomic Co-N5/NC and Co-N4/NC, respectively. According to the thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) results (Figure S1), the relatively lower thermal stability of CoPh, in comparison with that of CoPc, is conducive to breaking the symmetric coordination of square-planar Co(II) precursors.

nodes.name: CoPc-Phen axial coordination and pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: NC octahedrons derived from ZIF-8 used as support. CoPc (cobalt phthalocyanine) with high thermal stability, axially coordinated with 1,10-phenanthroline (Phen), pyrolyzed to form single-atomic Co-N4/NC. High thermal stability maintains planar Co-N4 coordination.
nodes.source_text: The NC octahedrons derived from zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-8) were used as support for CoPh and CoPc axially coordinated with 1,10-phenanthroline (Phen) and were subsequently pyrolyzed to single-atomic Co-N5/NC and Co-N4/NC, respectively. Cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) with high thermal stability enables the well-remained planar Co-N4 coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: No Co nanoparticles found on Co-N5/NC and Co-N4/NC; ~9.9 nm nanoparticles observed on CoNPs/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed that no Co nanoparticles were found on Co-N5/NC and Co-N4/NC, in comparison with the ~9.9 nm nanoparticles observed on CoNPs/NC (Figures 1b-d and S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Even distribution of N and Co elements confirmed in Co-N5/NC and Co-N4/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping attached on TEM further confirmed the even distribution of N and Co elements in Co-N5/NC and Co-N4/NC (Figures 1e and S4a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Bright spots detected indicating highly dispersive Co atoms on NC supports of both Co-N5/NC and Co-N4/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Bright spots (yellow circles) were detected in the spherical aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) images of both Co-N5/NC and Co-N4/NC (Figures 1f and S4b), implying the highly dispersive Co atoms on the NC supports.

nodes.characterization_summary: Three samples displayed similar Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface areas.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The three samples displayed similar Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface areas (Figure S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: ID/IG ratios close for Co-N5/NC, Co-N4/NC, and CoNPs/NC, indicating similar defect densities of NC supports.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ID/IG ratios of Raman spectra of Co-N5/NC, Co-N4/NC, and CoNPs/NC were close, indicating that the defect densities of NC supports were similar over the three samples (Figure S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: Two broad peaks at 2θ = 25.0° and 43.6° associated with (002) and (100) of graphite; no Co-related diffraction peak observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Their powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns were shown in Figure 1g. There were two broad peaks at 2θ = 25.0° and 43.6° associated with the (002) and (100) of graphite. No Co-related diffraction peak was observed for the high dispersion or low content of Co on the NC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows changes in pre-edge peak intensity for Co-N5/NC indicating asymmetric electron distribution; oxidation state between Co2+ and Co3+ for Co-N5/NC, more positive for Co-N4/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the Co K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra (Figure 2a), there were changes in the pre-edge peak intensity, resulting from the 1s to 3d as well as 1s to 4p transition of electrons in Co-N5/NC compare with Co-N4/NC and CoPc reference... The blue area of the inset image in Figure 2a displayed that the near-edge absorption energy of Co-N5/NC located within those of CoO and Co2O3, suggesting the oxidation state between Co2+ and Co3+. Co-N4/NC exhibited slightly higher absorption energy than Co2O3, indicative of a more positive oxidation state than that of Co-N5/NC.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows no Co-Co path confirming single-atomic dispersion; Co-N coordination shell at ~1.41 Å for Co-N5/NC (CN≈5) vs ~1.47 Å for Co-N4/NC (CN≈4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: To picture the local coordination environment, the Fourier-transformed k3-weighted extended XAFS (FT-EXAFS) was assigned to the Co-N first coordination shell (Figures 2b and S8-S12). As shown in Figure 2b, there was no Co-Co path in either Co-N4/NC or Co-N5/NC... The Co-N path of Co-N5/NC (~1.41Å) was smaller than that of Co-N4/NC (~1.47Å) and CoPc reference (~1.48Å)... According to the fitting EXAFS data, the coordination number of Co was closer to 5 for Co-N5/NC and 4 for Co-N4/NC (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: N1s profiles contain Py-N, Pr-N, Gr-N, N-O species with different contents; Py-N and Pr-N peaks shift to higher binding energy after Co anchoring, more so for Co-N4/NC than Co-N5/NC; confirms Co-N coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in XPS (Figure 2d), the N profiles of Co-N5/NC and Co-N4/NC contained pyridinic-N (Py-N), pyrrolic-N (Pr-N), graphitic-N (Gr-N), and oxidized-N (N-O) species, but their contents were different... the Py-N and Pr-N signals of Co-N4/NC shifted toward higher binding energies than those of Co-N5/NC.
